correctness.rationale: All ranks n>=2 and all points of the continuous hypersimplex are covered. The C_n cube is a genuine face of actual Catalan matroid bases. Equation (1) is the exact Euclidean projection distance to that cube; binary combinatorial counts bound it sharply at R_n^2=floor((n+3)/2). A Dyck witness excludes unordered equality candidates, and a pairwise sorted normal certificate verifies that the remaining one/two candidates project to C_n within P_n. Convexity reduces continuous maximizers to the hull of the vertex maximizers; the common normal certifies the full edge when n is even. Exact support inequalities and independent numerical QP on all 1272 hypersimplex vertices for n=2..6 support the proof; these tests are not mistaken for an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The natural geometric error of enforcing Dyck ballot constraints on the canonical constant-weight polytope is fully solved, including an exact sqrt(n)-scale formula, explicit sharp projections on an exposed high-dimensional cube, and a parity-dependent change in dimension of the complete farthest-point locus. The extreme-point classification is not a routine face count, cheap normalization check, or arbitrary finite slice; it identifies precisely the worst perturbations for every rank and provides a sharp benchmark for the broader lattice-path matroid family.
